description:
# Goal

Restore the 00181 causal ratchet after the reactive executable-effect cutover by pinning the cache-hit work that the new formula graph actually performs. Preserve the simple stack pull protocol, exact structured identities, and the green push boundary before publishing fz-tfn.10.

# Proven behavior

CI run 33895141634 on fz-tfn.8 passed all 1,786 library tests, the 525-test serial fixture matrix, 28 other fz2_cli tests, and lint, then failed `the_drain_arbiter_publishes_readiness_only_movement_and_attributes_every_evaluation`. The exact product tuple was `(408, 408, 408, 0, 19, 0)` versus the pre-cutover expectation `(408, 408, 408, 0, 18, 0)`.

This is deterministic expectation drift, not coverage or process-global nondeterminism. At exact commit bd666caa6, twelve ordinary fresh compiler processes and four llvm-cov-instrumented fresh compiler processes all produced 19 cache hits with the same ordered structured cache-hit identities. The exact standalone fz2_cli test reproduces 19 both normally and through cargo llvm-cov. Parent fz-tfn.7 commit 78aef7e08 produces 18 in four fresh processes.

The one-count delta is explained by the change of authority in fz-tfn.8. The old cone mini-compiler left one cached `ExecutableEffects(Enum.reduce/3)` retry. The reactive formulas leave two cached retries for the real two-member recursive group: `ExecutableEffects(List.reduce_cont/3)` and `ExecutableEffects(List.reduce_step/3)`. `List.reduce_cont/3` first waits on `List.reduce_step/3`; that member waits back on `List.reduce_cont/3`; the second reduce-cont evaluation closes the two-member group and atomically settles both at generation 1 with one group id. The pull stack then resumes each independently suspended member request, and both read their already-published memo values. The old Enum.reduce hit disappears, so the net is +1. Settlements, distinct generations, changed/unchanged outcomes, displacements, scheduler tallies, backend result, and runtime behavior do not move.

This is not the readiness-EOF race in fz-tfn.28 and is not the untriggered producer retry defect in fz-tfn.32. A cache hit is a request that does not evaluate a producer; these two requests have exact preceding waits and settlements.

# Strategy and TDD

1. Use the existing failing 00181 fz2_cli assertion as the RED; do not manufacture a production change for a stale expectation.
2. Replace the pre-cutover aggregate expectation with the exact post-cutover tuple and additionally pin the two structured executable-effect cache-hit identities to `List.reduce_cont/3` and `List.reduce_step/3`, each exactly once.
3. Derive those names only through the public trace canonical-reporting projection. Raw `ProductKey` remains the semantic authority; canonical strings remain confined to cross-process test reporting.
4. Document why atomic recursive-group settlement leaves one cache-only suspended request per member and why this is not a producer retry.
5. Prove the exact standalone test normally and under llvm-cov, the cross-process causal/backend test, full library, serial fixture matrix, full fz2_cli, formatting, strict clippy, and CI.

# Acceptance

The 00181 test proves the exact product tuple `(408, 408, 408, 0, 19, 0)` and the exact two executable-effect cache-hit identities/counts. Repeated ordinary and llvm-cov executions agree. No production scheduling code, retry/sleep, multiple accepted baseline, ExecutableEffects exception, or display/canonical string semantic identity is introduced. Documentation describes the reactive formula/group trace. All gates are green, and fz-tfn.10 remains unpushed until this ticket is closed and its CI succeeds.
title: Pin 00181 reactive effect-group cache-hit causality
